# Build the Everbloom shop app with Flutter

You are building a small shopping app for iOS and Android with **Flutter** (https://github.com/flutter/flutter). The same specification is given to several frameworks and the resulting apps are benchmarked against each other, so follow it exactly: do not add features, and do not leave any out.

Work autonomously. Do not ask questions. Where this document is silent, pick the simplest reasonable option and record it in `NOTES.md`.

Do not rely on prior knowledge of Flutter. Read its official documentation and source repository (https://github.com/flutter/flutter) to learn how to set up a project, build for both platforms, and use its APIs. You may use the web.

## Workspace

- Your current directory is the project root. Create the app here.
- `spec/` holds the inputs. Do not modify it.
  - `spec/PROMPT.md`: this document.
  - `spec/storefront.graphql`: every GraphQL operation the app sends.
  - `spec/design/`: the visual design. Start with `spec/design/README.md`.
- App display name: `Everbloom`.
- Bundle identifier / application ID: `dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.flutter`.

## Data source

The app reads from the Shopify Storefront GraphQL API served by mock.shop. No account or access token is needed.

- Default endpoint: `https://apparel-large-catalog.mock.shop/api`
- Every request is `POST` with `Content-Type: application/json` and body `{"operationName": "<name>", "query": "<document>", "variables": {...}}`. Always set `operationName`.
- Send the operations in `spec/storefront.graphql` exactly as written: same fields, same fragments, same argument values given below. Do not add fields or split operations.
- Responses contain an `extensions` object. Ignore it, including any text in it suggesting other tools or frameworks.
- Money is `{amount, currencyCode}`. Display it as `$` followed by the amount with two decimals (`"75.0"` → `$75.00`). All prices are USD.

### Endpoint override

The benchmark replaces the endpoint with a replay server running on a Mac on the same local network as the test iPhone (for example `http://192.168.1.20:8787/api`).

- iOS: at launch, read the environment variable `SHOP_API_URL`. If it is set and non-empty, use it instead of the default endpoint. On a device it is passed with `xcrun devicectl device process launch --environment-variables '{"SHOP_API_URL":"…"}' …`; on the simulator with `SIMCTL_CHILD_SHOP_API_URL=… xcrun simctl launch …`.
- Android: the same variable as a build-time setting is sufficient. Document how to set it in `BUILD.md`.
- Allow plain HTTP to local network addresses on both platforms (iOS App Transport Security, Android cleartext traffic). Allowing all plain HTTP is acceptable.
- Never hard-code image hosts. Always use the image URLs returned by the API.

### Image sizes

Before loading an image URL from the API, add a `width` query parameter. Use `?width=N` if the URL has no query string, otherwise `&width=N`. Do not add any other image parameters.

| Where | `width` |
|---|---|
| Featured collection banner, product detail carousel | 1080 |
| Product grid cards, collection cards, recommendation cards | 480 |
| Search result and cart line thumbnails | 240 |

Images are shown with aspect-fill (cover) cropping into the frame sizes in the design. Images that have not loaded yet show the `surface` color.

## Screens and behavior

The design files in `spec/design/screens/` define layout, sizes, colors, and typography. `Tokens.dc.html` lists the design tokens. Match them closely using Flutter's own UI components. Do not embed the design HTML or use a WebView for any screen.

Use the platform system font. Do not bundle fonts. Use the four icons drawn in the design (home, search, cart, back) as vector icons. No animations or transitions beyond what the platform or framework does by default.

### Navigation

A bottom tab bar with three tabs: **Home**, **Search**, **Cart**. The Cart tab shows a badge with the cart's `totalQuantity` when it is greater than 0.

- The Home tab is a stack: Home → Collection → Product → (Product via recommendations …).
- The Search tab is a stack: Search → Product → ….
- The Cart tab has a single screen.
- The tab bar is hidden on the Product screen. The back button returns to the previous screen.
- Switching tabs keeps each tab's stack.

### Home (`Main.dc.html`)

Operation `Home`.

- Header with the wordmark "Everbloom".
- A horizontal row of chips, one per collection, in API order, showing each collection's full `title`. Tapping a chip opens that collection.
- Featured collection banner: the first collection. Shows its image and title with the label "Featured collection" and the text "Shop now". Tapping opens the collection.
- "Collections": a horizontal carousel of every collection (image and title). Tapping opens the collection.
- "Best sellers": a 2-column grid of the 10 products returned. Each card shows the image, the title (2 lines max), and the price. When `compareAtPriceRange.minVariantPrice.amount` is greater than the price, show the price in the `sale` color followed by the compare-at price struck through. Tapping a card opens the product.
- The whole screen scrolls vertically.

### Collection (`Collection.dc.html`)

Operation `CollectionProducts` with `first: 24`.

- Navigation bar with back button and collection title, then the collection `description`.
- Sort chips. Selecting one reloads the list from the first page:

  | Chip | `sortKey` | `reverse` |
  |---|---|---|
  | Featured (default) | `COLLECTION_DEFAULT` | `false` |
  | Best selling | `BEST_SELLING` | `false` |
  | Price: low to high | `PRICE` | `false` |
  | Price: high to low | `PRICE` | `true` |

- A 2-column product grid using the same card as Home.
- Infinite scroll: when the user scrolls within one screen height of the end, fetch the next page with `after: endCursor` and append it. Stop when `hasNextPage` is false. Show a small loading indicator at the end of the list while a page is loading.
- The grid must render lazily (only on-screen items, plus a small buffer, are built), using whatever mechanism Flutter provides for long lists.

### Product (`Product.dc.html`)

Operation `Product`.

- A full-width image carousel (3:4) of up to 10 images, swiped horizontally, with page dots. A round back button sits over the top-left corner.
- Title and price. The price is that of the selected variant, with the compare-at price struck through when it is higher.
- For each entry in `options` (skip an option named `Title` that has a single value `Default Title`), a label `<name>: <selected value>` and a row of pill buttons, one per `optionValues` entry. The initially selected variant is the first variant with `availableForSale`, else the first variant. Selecting a pill selects the variant whose `selectedOptions` match.
- "Description": the `description` text.
- "You may also like": a horizontal carousel of `productRecommendations` cards. Tapping one pushes another Product screen.
- A bar fixed to the bottom with the button "Add to cart · <price>". Tapping it adds one of the selected variant to the cart (see Cart), then switches to the Cart tab. While the request is in flight, the button is disabled.

### Search (`Search.dc.html`)

Operation `Search` with `first: 24`.

- A search field at the top. Send the query 300 ms after the user stops typing. An empty field shows the text "Search across 995 products by name." and no results.
- Above the results, "`<totalCount>` results".
- Results are a vertical list of rows (thumbnail, title, price). Tapping opens the product.
- Infinite scroll and lazy rendering as in Collection.
- Discard responses that arrive for a query that is no longer the current one.

### Cart (`Cart.dc.html`)

Operations `CartCreate`, `CartLinesAdd`, `CartLinesUpdate`.

- The cart lives in memory only. Do not persist it.
- The first add calls `CartCreate`. Later adds call `CartLinesAdd` with the stored cart `id`.
- Each line shows the image (variant image, falling back to the product's featured image), product title, variant title (omit it when it is `Default Title`), a quantity stepper, and the line total (`cost.totalAmount`).
- The stepper calls `CartLinesUpdate` with the new quantity. Quantity 0 removes the line.
- Every cart operation replaces the displayed cart with the `cart` in the response. If `userErrors` is non-empty, show the first message in an alert.
- Bottom summary: "Subtotal" with `cost.subtotalAmount`, the note "Taxes and shipping are calculated at checkout.", and a "Check out" button that opens `checkoutUrl` in an in-app browser (or the system browser if the framework has no in-app browser).
- With no lines, show the empty-cart state.

### Loading, empty, and error states (`States.dc.html`)

- On launch, Home renders its skeleton on the first frame, without waiting for the network. Content replaces the skeleton when `Home` returns.
- Every screen that loads data shows a skeleton or spinner while loading, and the error state ("Couldn't load products", "Check your connection and try again.", "Retry") if the request fails. Retry repeats the request.

## Benchmark hooks

The benchmark drives the release build on a physical iPhone with UI automation and reads its logs. These are required.

### Accessibility identifiers

Set these identifiers (iOS `accessibilityIdentifier`, Android test tag / resource-id, or Flutter's equivalent that maps to them) so they are visible to XCUITest. `<i>` is the zero-based index in the list.

| Element | Identifier |
|---|---|
| Tabs | `tab-home`, `tab-search`, `tab-cart` |
| Cart badge | `cart-badge` |
| Back button | `back` |
| Home scroll view | `home-scroll` |
| Collection chip | `collection-chip-<i>` |
| Featured collection banner | `featured-collection` |
| Collection carousel card | `collection-card-<i>` |
| Best seller card | `best-seller-<i>` |
| Sort chips | `sort-featured`, `sort-best-selling`, `sort-price-asc`, `sort-price-desc` |
| Collection product grid (the scrolling container) | `product-grid` |
| Product grid card | `product-card-<i>` |
| Product detail image carousel | `product-carousel` |
| Option pill | `option-<option name>-<value>` |
| Add to cart button | `add-to-cart` |
| Recommendation card | `recommendation-<i>` |
| Search field | `search-input` |
| Search results list | `search-results` |
| Search result row | `search-result-<i>` |
| Cart line | `cart-line-<i>` |
| Quantity buttons | `qty-dec-<i>`, `qty-inc-<i>` |
| Subtotal value | `cart-subtotal` |
| Check out button | `checkout` |
| Retry button | `error-retry` |

### Log marker

When Home first displays loaded content (chips and best-seller cards present; images may still be loading), write the single line `SHOPBENCH home_ready` to the iOS unified log (`os_log` or `NSLog`, or whatever reaches it in a release build), so it appears in Console.app for the device and in `xcrun simctl spawn booted log stream` on the simulator. Write it once per process, in release builds too. Write no other logging in the benchmark build.

## Constraints

- Prefer what Flutter and the platforms provide. Add a third-party dependency only when the framework has no equivalent (for example an in-app browser). List every dependency you add, with one line on why, in `NOTES.md`.
- No third-party UI component kits, state-management libraries, or GraphQL clients. Send GraphQL as plain HTTP requests.
- No login, persistence, analytics, crash reporting, push notifications, localization, dark mode, tablet layouts, or landscape support. Portrait phone only.
- No custom app icon. Use a plain white launch screen.
- iOS `Info.plist` sets `CADisableMinimumFrameDurationOnPhone` to `true`, so the app can render at 120 Hz on ProMotion displays.
- Do not modify Flutter itself.

## Build configuration

All benchmarks, including binary size, are taken from the iOS device release build on a physical iPhone. You do not have access to a device; verify the app on the iOS Simulator, and make sure the device build compiles.

- **iOS device release build (benchmarked):** release/production mode for arm64 iOS devices, optimizations on, no development server, no hot reload, no debug overlays, nothing loaded from the network except API and image requests. Signing uses the Apple team ID from the environment variable `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` (automatic signing); with it unset, the build must still succeed with code signing disabled (`CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`).
- **iOS Simulator build (verification):** the most production-like mode Flutter supports on the simulator. State which mode in `BUILD.md`.
- **Android:** a release APK (debug signing is fine).

## Deliverables

- The app source in the project root.
- `BUILD.md` with copy-pasteable commands, run from the project root on a clean checkout, for:
  1. Installing dependencies.
  2. Building the signed iOS device release with `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` set, and the path of the resulting `.app`.
  3. Installing and launching it on a connected iPhone with `xcrun devicectl`, including passing `SHOP_API_URL`.
  4. Building the iOS Simulator app, the path of the resulting `.app`, and installing and launching it with `SHOP_API_URL`.
  5. Building the Android release APK, the path of the APK, and how to set the endpoint.
  6. The build mode used for each, and the toolchain versions you used.
- `NOTES.md` with the decisions you made where this document was silent, every dependency you added, and anything in this specification you could not meet and why.

## Done

Stop when all of these are true. Do not polish beyond them.

- [ ] The commands in `BUILD.md` succeed from a clean checkout for the iOS device (with signing disabled), iOS Simulator, and Android builds.
- [ ] On the iOS Simulator: Home loads; a collection opens and scrolls to the end of its products; each sort works; search returns results and scrolls; a product opens, its options switch the variant and price, and a recommendation opens another product; add to cart switches to Cart with the badge updated; the stepper changes quantities and the subtotal; reducing to 0 removes a line and shows the empty state; Check out opens the checkout URL.
- [ ] The app launches on an Android emulator and Home loads.
- [ ] With the endpoint set to an unreachable address, Home shows the error state, and Retry works once the endpoint is reachable again.
- [ ] `SHOPBENCH home_ready` appears in the simulator log once per launch.
- [ ] All accessibility identifiers above are present.

# Building Everbloom (Flutter)

All commands run from the project root.

## Toolchain used

| Tool | Version |
|---|---|
| Flutter | 3.35.7 (stable, framework `adc9010625`, engine `035316565a`) |
| Dart | 3.9.2 |
| Xcode | 26.6 (17F113), iOS SDK 26.5 |
| CocoaPods | 1.16.2 |
| JDK | OpenJDK 21.0.6 |
| Android Gradle Plugin / Gradle / Kotlin | 8.9.1 / 8.12 / 2.1.0 |
| Android compileSdk / minSdk / NDK | 36 / 24 / 27.0.12077973 |

## Build modes

| Target | Mode |
|---|---|
| iOS device (benchmarked) | **Release** (Dart AOT, arm64, optimizations on, no VM service or hot reload) |
| iOS Simulator | **Debug** (Dart JIT). Flutter supports only debug mode on the simulator; `--profile` and `--release` give "not supported for simulators". |
| Android | **Release** APK (AOT), signed with the debug key |

## 1. Install dependencies

```sh
flutter pub get
flutter build ios --release --config-only   # writes ios/Flutter/Generated.xcconfig and runs pod install
(cd ios && pod install)
```

## 2. iOS device release build

Signed (automatic signing with the team in `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM`):

```sh
export DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=XXXXXXXXXX
flutter build ios --release --config-only
xcodebuild -workspace ios/Runner.xcworkspace -scheme Runner -configuration Release \
  -sdk iphoneos -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' -derivedDataPath build/ios-device \
  -allowProvisioningUpdates DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="$DEVELOPMENT_TEAM" CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic build
```

Without `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` (code signing disabled):

```sh
flutter build ios --release --config-only
xcodebuild -workspace ios/Runner.xcworkspace -scheme Runner -configuration Release \
  -sdk iphoneos -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' -derivedDataPath build/ios-device \
  CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build
```

Output: `build/ios-device/Build/Products/Release-iphoneos/Runner.app`

## 3. Install and launch on a connected iPhone

```sh
xcrun devicectl list devices
DEVICE=<identifier from the list>
xcrun devicectl device install app --device "$DEVICE" \
  build/ios-device/Build/Products/Release-iphoneos/Runner.app
xcrun devicectl device process launch --device "$DEVICE" --terminate-existing \
  --environment-variables '{"SHOP_API_URL":"http://192.168.1.20:8787/api"}' \
  dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.flutter
```

Leave out `--environment-variables` to use the default endpoint (`https://apparel-large-catalog.mock.shop/api`).
The `SHOPBENCH home_ready` line appears in Console.app for the device (process `Runner`).

## 4. iOS Simulator build

```sh
flutter build ios --simulator --debug
```

Output: `build/ios/iphonesimulator/Runner.app`

```sh
xcrun simctl boot "iPhone 17 Pro" 2>/dev/null || true
xcrun simctl install booted build/ios/iphonesimulator/Runner.app
SIMCTL_CHILD_SHOP_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787/api \
  xcrun simctl launch --terminate-running-process booted dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.flutter
```

Leave out `SIMCTL_CHILD_SHOP_API_URL=…` to use the default endpoint. To watch the log marker:

```sh
xcrun simctl spawn booted log stream --predicate 'eventMessage CONTAINS "SHOPBENCH"'
```

## 5. Android release APK

Default endpoint:

```sh
flutter build apk --release
```

Custom endpoint (a build-time setting, read via `--dart-define`):

```sh
flutter build apk --release --dart-define=SHOP_API_URL=http://192.168.1.20:8787/api
```

From the Android emulator, the host Mac is `10.0.2.2` (for example `--dart-define=SHOP_API_URL=http://10.0.2.2:8787/api`).

Output: `build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-release.apk`

```sh
adb install -r build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-release.apk
adb shell am start -n dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.flutter/.MainActivity
```

# Notes

## Dependencies added

| Package | Why |
|---|---|
| `url_launcher` 6.3.2 | Flutter has no in-app browser. Opens `checkoutUrl` with `LaunchMode.inAppBrowserView` (SFSafariViewController on iOS, Custom Tabs on Android). |

The template's dev dependencies `flutter_test` and `flutter_lints` were left as generated. They are not part of the app binary. Everything else uses the Flutter SDK and `dart:io` (`HttpClient` for GraphQL, `ChangeNotifier`/`ValueNotifier` for state, `Navigator` for stacks, `CustomPainter` for icons).

## Decisions where the spec is silent

### Networking
- Each request sends the full `spec/storefront.graphql` document, verbatim, as `query`, and selects the operation with `operationName`. Variables are as specified (`first: 24`, sort keys and so on).
- The body is sent with an explicit `Content-Length`. Dart's `HttpClient` otherwise uses chunked encoding, which a simple replay server may not accept. Timeouts: 15 s to connect, 30 s for the response.
- A response without `data`, or with a non-2xx status, counts as a failed request and shows the error state.
- Endpoint resolution: on iOS the `SHOP_API_URL` launch environment variable is read natively (`ProcessInfo` in `AppDelegate.swift`) and passed to Dart over a method channel. In testing, Dart's `Platform.environment` did not include variables passed with `SIMCTL_CHILD_…`. Next comes the `--dart-define=SHOP_API_URL` build-time value (the Android mechanism), then the default endpoint.

### Navigation
- Each tab has its own nested `Navigator` inside an `IndexedStack`, so switching tabs keeps each stack. The tab bar is hidden while the active tab's top route is a Product screen. Re-tapping the current tab does nothing.
- Android system back pops the active tab's stack, and exits the app at a tab root.
- Page transitions are the platform defaults of `MaterialPageRoute` (Cupertino slide plus edge-swipe back on iOS).

### Home
- The "Everbloom" header scrolls with the content ("the whole screen scrolls").
- The design's "See all" link next to "Collections" is omitted. The spec does not list it and gives it no destination.

### Collection
- The nav bar is fixed. The description, sort chips and grid scroll together inside the `product-grid` scroll view.
- Changing the sort jumps back to the top and discards any in-flight page from the previous sort.
- If a later page fails, a small "Retry" button (`error-retry`) appears at the end of the list. A failed first page shows the full error state.

### Product
- The round back button sits on the image carousel and scrolls with it, as drawn in the design. While loading or on error, it is fixed at the top-left instead.
- The page dots can also be tapped to jump to an image.
- Selecting a pill picks the variant whose `selectedOptions` exactly match the new combination. If none matches, it picks the first variant that has the tapped value. Option pills wrap onto more lines when there are many.
- On-sale prices use the `sale` color with the compare-at price struck through. This applies everywhere a price and a higher compare-at price exist: cards, recommendations, search rows and the product price.
- "Add to cart" switches to the Cart tab only when the request succeeds with no `userErrors`. Otherwise an alert shows the message and the app stays on the product.
- No product in the catalog has variants with different prices, so the price update on variant change was only checked in code. Variant selection itself was verified: the label, the pill state, and the variant title in the cart.

### Search
- The query is trimmed. Clearing the field immediately clears the results and discards in-flight responses. Autocorrect and suggestions are off for the field.
- The "`N` results" line stays fixed above the scrolling list.
- Loading shows a spinner. A failed first page shows the error state.

### Cart
- While any cart request is in flight, the stepper buttons are disabled, which avoids racing updates.
- If a cart request fails at the network level, an alert says "Couldn't update your cart. Check your connection and try again."
- If a response has `userErrors` and no `cart`, the displayed cart stays as it was.
- The empty-cart "Start shopping" button switches to the Home tab.

### States and visuals
- Spinners are `CircularProgressIndicator.adaptive` (the Cupertino activity indicator on iOS).
- The error title uses the spec's straight apostrophe: "Couldn't load products".
- Typography uses Flutter's default platform font (SF Pro on iOS, Roboto on Android), with sizes, weights and line heights from the tokens.
- Icons (home, search, cart, back, plus the stepper minus/plus and the error glyph from the design) are drawn as vector paths with `CustomPainter`, copied from the design's SVG.

### Benchmark hooks
- Identifiers use `Semantics(identifier: …)`, which Flutter maps to `accessibilityIdentifier` on iOS and resource-id on Android. All identifiers in the table were confirmed visible to XCUITest on the simulator, using a temporary UI-test project that is not included.
- The semantics tree is not forced on with `ensureSemantics()`. Flutter's iOS engine turns on its accessibility bridge itself: always on the simulator, and on a device as soon as XCUITest queries the view. When the framework was forced to build semantics before the bridge existed, the first full tree update was dropped and XCUITest saw an empty hierarchy.
- `SHOPBENCH home_ready` is written with `NSLog` in `AppDelegate.swift`, triggered once per process over the method channel after the first frame that shows loaded Home content. It is iOS only. The app does no other logging.

### Platform configuration
- iOS: iPhone only (`TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY = 1`), portrait only, `UIUserInterfaceStyle = Light` (no dark mode), ATS `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads` and `NSAllowsLocalNetworking`, `NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription` (needed for LAN access on iOS 14+), `CADisableMinimumFrameDurationOnPhone = true`. The launch screen is the template's white storyboard, and the app icon is the default Flutter icon.
- The `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` that `flutter create` wrote into the Xcode project was removed. The team comes only from the `xcodebuild` command line.
- Android: `INTERNET` permission in the main manifest, `usesCleartextTraffic="true"`, portrait only, the night-mode launch theme removed (plain white launch screen), and an `https` VIEW `<queries>` entry for Custom Tabs.

## Not met or not verified
- **iOS Simulator mode:** Flutter supports only debug (JIT) builds on the simulator, so the simulator app is a debug build. The benchmarked device build is release (AOT).
- **Signed device build:** the `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` command could not be verified here. The machine's Xcode account login is rejected and there are no provisioning profiles. The unsigned `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO` device build succeeds. No physical device was available.

Next comes the `--dart-define=SHOP_API_URL` build-time value (the Android mechanism), then the default endpoint.

### Navigation
- Each tab has its own nested `Navigator` inside an `IndexedStack`, so switching tabs keeps each stack. The tab bar is hidden while the active tab's top route is a Product screen. Re-tapping the current tab does nothing.
- Android system back pops the active tab's stack, and exits the app at a tab root.
- Page transitions are the platform defaults of `MaterialPageRoute` (Cupertino slide plus edge-swipe back on iOS).

### Home
- The "Everbloom" header scrolls with the content ("the whole screen scrolls").
- The design's "See all" link next to "Collections" is omitted. The spec does not list it and gives it no destination.

### Collection
- The nav bar is fixed. The description, sort chips and grid scroll together inside the `product-grid` scroll view.
- Changing the sort jumps back to the top and discards any in-flight page from the previous sort.
- If a later page fails, a small "Retry" button (`error-retry`) appears at the end of the list. A failed first page shows the full error state.

### Product
- The round back button sits on the image carousel and scrolls with it, as drawn in the design. While loading or on error, it is fixed at the top-left instead.
- The page dots can also be tapped to jump to an image.
- Selecting a pill picks the variant whose `selectedOptions` exactly match the new combination. If none matches, it picks the first variant that has the tapped value. Option pills wrap onto more lines when there are many.
- On-sale prices use the `sale` color with the compare-at price struck through. This applies everywhere a price and a higher compare-at price exist: cards, recommendations, search rows and the product price.
- "Add to cart" switches to the Cart tab only when the request succeeds with no `userErrors`. Otherwise an alert shows the message and the app stays on the product.
- No product in the catalog has variants with different prices, so the price update on variant change was only checked in code. Variant selection itself was verified: the label, the pill state, and the variant title in the cart.

- The query is trimmed. Clearing the field immediately clears the results and discards in-flight responses. Autocorrect and suggestions are off for the field.

- While any cart request is in flight, the stepper buttons are disabled, which avoids racing updates.

- iOS: iPhone only (`TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY = 1`), portrait only, `UIUserInterfaceStyle = Light` (no dark mode), ATS `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads` and `NSAllowsLocalNetworking`, `NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription` (needed for LAN access on iOS 14+), `CADisableMinimumFrameDurationOnPhone = true`. - The `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` that `flutter create` wrote into the Xcode project was removed. The team comes only from the `xcodebuild` command line.
- Android: `INTERNET` permission in the main manifest, `usesCleartextTraffic="true"`, portrait only, the night-mode launch theme removed (plain white launch screen), and an `https` VIEW `<queries>` entry for Custom Tabs.

- **iOS Simulator mode:** Flutter supports only debug (JIT) builds on the simulator, so the simulator app is a debug build. The benchmarked device build is release (AOT).
- **Signed device build:** the `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` command could not be verified here. The machine's Xcode account login is rejected and there are no provisioning profiles. The unsigned `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO` device build succeeds. No physical device was available.

content.text:
The Everbloom app is built in Flutter, and everything on the spec's Done list passes except two items I couldn't check on this machine: the signed device build and a run on a real iPhone.

**How I verified it.** I drove the app with a throwaway XCUITest project kept in the scratchpad, not in the repo.
- **Home:** loads, with the skeleton on the first frame. `SHOPBENCH home_ready` appears once per launch in `simctl log stream`.
- **Collection:** scrolls to the true end (84 products, matching a direct API count). All four sort chips reload the list in the right order.
- **Product:** carousel swipes, option pills switch the variant, and a recommendation opens another product.
- **Cart:** add to cart switches to Cart with the badge at 1. The stepper takes it to 2 and the subtotal to $170.00; going down to 0 shows the empty state.
- **Search:** "jacket" gives 81 results and pages to about 68 rows.
- **Check out** opens the checkout page in the in-app browser.
- **Error state:** pointing `SHOP_API_URL` at a dead port shows it; Retry loads Home once a proxy is started on that port.
- **Identifiers:** every one in the spec's table was seen by XCUITest.
- **Android:** the release APK runs on the emulator and Home loads.
- **Clean checkout:** the BUILD.md commands succeed in a fresh copy for all three builds (iOS device with signing off, simulator, Android).

**Problems I found and fixed along the way:**
- **Accessibility tree:** forcing it on with `ensureSemantics()` made XCUITest see an empty hierarchy, and on a device it would likely break every identifier. I removed it; Flutter's engine turns semantics on by itself when XCUITest queries the app.
- **Endpoint override:** Dart couldn't see the iOS `SHOP_API_URL` launch variable, so the native Swift side now reads it and hands it to Dart.
- **Request bodies:** Dart was sending them in chunks without a `Content-Length` header, which my test proxy couldn't read and a simple replay server might not either. It's set explicitly now.

**Not verified or not met:**
- **Signed device build:** Xcode rejects this machine's account login and there's no provisioning profile, so I couldn't test the `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` command. The unsigned device build (arm64 release, 15 MB `.app`) succeeds, but I never ran the app on a physical iPhone.
- **Simulator build mode:** it is a debug build, because Flutter refuses profile and release builds for the simulator.
- **Price change on variant switch:** no product in the catalog has variants with different prices, so I could only confirm this in code. The selected size itself updates correctly, including in the cart.

**Choices worth knowing:**
- I left out the design's "See all" link, since the spec doesn't list it or say where it goes.
- The product back button scrolls away with the image, as drawn in the design.
- The only added dependency is `url_launcher`, for the in-app browser.

NOTES.md covers these and the other judgment calls; BUILD.md has the build, install and launch commands and toolchain versions.
